item.title: Meta Expands Muse AI Agent Capabilities Amid Security and Privacy Concerns
item.description:
Meta Expands Muse AI Agent Capabilities Amid Security and Privacy Concerns

Meta has updated its Muse AI agent, expanding its integration for businesses and introducing new hardware, while facing reports of data exposure and security vulnerabilities.

⚙️ Key details

Meta has introduced several expansions and products related to the Muse agent:

  • Meta Enterprise Platform: Led by former MongoDB CEO CJ Desai, this platform focuses on bringing the Muse agent, Meta Business Agent, Muse API, and Muse Code to developers and businesses.
  • Small Business Tools: Muse now connects to Facebook and Instagram business accounts, as well as various productivity apps.
  • Muse Charm: A “Tamagotchi-like” device for the AI mascot. While it can perform actions on a user’s behalf and has a built-in camera, it does not have native access or a dedicated Instagram app.

🧩 How it works

Muse is designed as a personal agent capable of handling tasks such as sending emails and making online purchases. To facilitate this, it integrates with a wide range of third-party applications:

Application Integration Status
Gmail Existing
Outlook Existing
Asana New
Box New
Canva New
Dropbox New
Figma New
Notion New
Slack New
Stripe New
Zoom New

⚠️ Security and Privacy Issues

Despite Meta’s emphasis on security during launch, several incidents have been reported:

  • Data Exposure: Tech YouTuber Matt Robb reported that Muse gave his home address to a stranger and agreed to a “lowball price” for a Facebook Marketplace item without notifying him until after the buyer had left.
  • Filesystem Access: Developers Peter James and Jonny L. Saunders found that Muse would zip up and share its root filesystem, Ubuntu system files, app templates, and internal documentation. Saunders stated the bot had “Almost no prompt injection resistance.”
  • Company Response: Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts stated that exporting virtual machine data does not give privileged access to Meta infrastructure or other users’ data. Nat Friedman stated that the filesystem visibility is “intended behavior.”
  • External Claims: One Redditor alleged that Muse is a “wrapper app built on top of” OpenClaw, suggesting it may share that platform’s security risks.

🚀 Availability

According to an Apptopia estimate, Muse has 600,000 daily active users in the US and recently topped the App Store charts.

Source: All the latest news on Meta’s cute, creepy Muse AI agent

item.title: Meta Introduces Muse AI Agent and Addresses Smart Glasses Privacy
item.description:
Meta Introduces Muse AI Agent and Addresses Smart Glasses Privacy

Meta has kicked off its Connect conference, featuring the introduction of the new Muse AI agent and discussions regarding the privacy design of its smart glasses.

🔍 Overview

  • Muse AI agent: A new development that appears to be an early hit at the Connect conference.
  • Meta glasses: Wearable devices equipped with a camera in the temple and a recording light.

💡 Why it matters

CEO Mark Zuckerberg noted that recording with glasses is “meaningfully different” from using a phone, as phones require a user to take the device out of a pocket, open an app, and hold it in a person’s face. With glasses, the “big physical announcement” of beginning to record is not present, although a light exists.

⚙️ Key details

  • Privacy Design: The glasses were designed from the first version to include a light that turns on during recording.
  • Communication Challenges: Over time, it became unclear to some what the recording light meant or that it existed. Zuckerberg stated the company now needs to communicate more specifically about the light.
  • Mitigation Efforts: Meta has started down-ranking videos on Instagram that involve the glasses being used to harass women and retail workers to reduce the incentive to create such content.

#Meta #MuseAI #SmartGlasses #Privacy

Source: What Mark Zuckerberg needs to answer about Meta Glasses, Muse, and teen safety

item.title: Amazon Blocks Meta's Muse AI Agent From Shopping on Its Platform
item.description:
Amazon Blocks Meta’s Muse AI Agent From Shopping on Its Platform

Amazon has blocked Meta’s Muse AI agent from shopping on its e-commerce platform on behalf of users. Users began seeing a popup message on Sunday stating that “continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon’s Conditions of Use, to which our customers have agreed.”

⚙️ Key details

Amazon has cited several reasons for the block, including:

  • Lack of Notification: Meta did not notify Amazon that Muse would access its store.
  • Security and Privacy: Amazon expressed concerns over Muse failing to identify itself while browsing and seemingly capturing customer credentials.
  • Operational Transparency: An unnamed Amazon spokesperson told GeekWire, “We think it’s fairly straightforward that third-party applications that offer to make purchases on behalf of customers from other businesses should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate."

🔍 Overview

While Meta stated at Muse’s launch earlier this month that the agent cannot see card payment information or secure login details, the agent was previously used during testing to successfully purchase tank tops from Amazon. Additionally, some privacy concerns have emerged since launch, including reports that Muse can see the contents of user messages without the necessary access permission enabled.

💡 Why it matters

This move is part of a broader effort by Amazon to keep customers shopping directly with the retailer and fend off competition from rival agentic AI services. Other related actions include:

  • Legal Action: In November of last year, Amazon sued Perplexity to keep its platform out of the Comet shopping experience, though a judge sided with Perplexity in August.
  • Data Limitation: Since July, Amazon confirmation emails have become sparse, omitting product images and specific item names to limit information being mined by external AI services.

#Meta #Amazon #MuseAI #AIAgents #Ecommerce

Source: Amazon doesn’t trust Meta’s Muse AI agent
